scope: Nine retained public workshops across three participant waves and three execution clusters.

event_intent_and_pivot.original_understanding: One 30-person cohort receiving three labs: 90 seat-environments.
event_intent_and_pivot.actual_requirement: Three 30-person cohorts, with every participant receiving all three labs and retaining access: 270 seat-environments.
event_intent_and_pivot.primary_cause: The event structure was communicated ambiguously; participant count, cohort count, labs per participant, and retention were not captured in one approved event manifest.
event_intent_and_pivot.flightpath_before_event: Disaster-recovery candidate only; not certified as a normal participant execution cluster.
event_intent_and_pivot.response: The operator recalculated demand, preserved the active wave, brought Flightpath into emergency execution service, provisioned the additional 180 seat-environments, and validated later waves under live-event time pressure.
event_intent_and_pivot.interpretation: The pivot demonstrates portability and AI-augmented SRE response, not prior production certification of Flightpath or fully automated elastic capacity.
event_intent_and_pivot.prevention: Require an approved versioned event manifest and capacity preview before reservation. Certified execution capacity, DR-reserved capacity, and uncertified theoretical capacity must be reported separately.

completion.statement: Participant completion was not consistently instrumented; a seat claim proves access, not successful completion of every lab checkpoint.
completion.available_proof: Representative synthetic, API, model, route, namespace-isolation, and manual participant checks exist, but they cannot be converted into 191 participant completion records.
completion.required: Emit versioned per-seat checkpoint, final outcome, duration, failure stage, catalog release, and anonymized cohort events.

clusters.name: Arena
clusters.note: Historical restarts across 23 pods, concentrated on gnr2.

clusters.name: Brutus
clusters.note: All active-seat pods ready at the snapshot.

clusters.name: Flightpath
clusters.note: All active-seat pods ready after the recorded image mitigation.

issues.statement: Mitigated means the participant path was protected temporarily; it is not durable closure.

telemetry.detail: Order, session, cluster, namespace, state, creation, and expiration records.
Claimed versus unclaimed counts by workshop; participant PII is excluded from the postmortem.
Pod readiness, route admission, restarts, namespace reconciliation, and orphan checks.
Replica readiness is known; per-seat requests, tokens, queues, latency, and rate limits are incomplete.
Representative checks exist, but every participant checkpoint and final outcome were not emitted.
Webhook/Kafka publication is best-effort without durable outbox, receipts, replay, or dead-letter handling.
No approved node, CPU, memory, storage, model, network, license, or labor rates are joined to usage.

known: 270 provisioned seats across nine seven-day workshop reservations
191 claimed and 79 unclaimed seats at the snapshot
Catalog, wave, cluster, workshop, session, namespace, and expiration attribution
Provisioned resources continue consuming capacity whether a seat is claimed or not
required: Node-hour and cluster shared-service rates, including hardware amortization, power, facilities, subscriptions, and support
Per-seat requested and actual CPU-, memory-, PVC-, and network-hours
Per-seat model requests, input/output tokens, accelerator or CPU inference time, queue time, retries, and failures
Registry, object-storage, egress, public-edge, identity, and observability costs
Operator and instructor labor minutes plus incident/support effort
A verified participant completion event so cost per completed lab is meaningful
financials.formula: Event cost = infrastructure + inference + storage/network + shared platform allocation + operator/instructor labor. Cost per claimed seat uses 191 as the denominator; cost per completed lab remains unavailable until completion telemetry exists.

estimate.status: planning estimate, not measured spend or an invoice

resource_basis.note: This excludes unmeasured OpenShift, control-plane, OVMS, storage, ingress, observability, and cluster headroom. Kubernetes requests are reservations, not actual utilization.

event_scenarios.name: Marginal infrastructure on already-owned hardware
event_scenarios.includes: Electricity/cooling allowance, storage/network activity, and minor shared-service consumption; excludes labor, hardware amortization, and subscriptions.

event_scenarios.name: Fully allocated seven-day infrastructure equivalent
event_scenarios.includes: Known CPU/memory reservations plus a platform/headroom allowance, storage, ingress, observability, and an allocated infrastructure rate.

event_scenarios.name: All-in pilot delivery
event_scenarios.includes: Fully allocated infrastructure plus approximately 80–180 hours of preparation, facilitation, incident response, and post-event work at a blended loaded enterprise rate.

event_unit_costs.note: The unclaimed share applies 79/270 to the infrastructure range and assumes claims did not rise after the snapshot. It is not automatically avoidable because event capacity was reserved in advance.

development.name: Estimated fully loaded development to date
development.basis: Approximately 160 hours of direct AI-accelerated work. At the modeled $140–$220 loaded enterprise rate, labor is $22.4K–$35.2K; the upper allowance includes development tooling and test infrastructure. This is an opportunity-cost view, not proof that this amount was paid incrementally.

development.name: Conventional replacement cost
development.basis: A hypothetical non-agentic cross-functional team reproducing the current backend, frontend, OpenShift/GitOps, identity, multi-cluster lifecycle, content, quality/evidence, and operations capability. This is replacement cost, not historical spend.

development.name: Additional investment to production roadmap completion
development.basis: Two or three parallel agentic workstreams plus product/architecture ownership through the April 2027 target, including HA/DR, security assessment, registry/supply chain, telemetry, FinOps, and migration work. Hardware expansion is excluded.

assumptions: The product owner reports approximately 160 hours of direct development effort to date.
Loaded enterprise engineering and specialist labor is modeled at $140–$220 per hour; actual internal transfer rates may differ.
At the BLS median software-developer wage, 160 hours is roughly $10.5K of salary-equivalent time before benefits and overhead.
The cloud-equivalent infrastructure range is a comparison lens, not a claim that the pilot ran on AWS.
Existing Intel hardware and Red Hat software/subscription acquisition costs were not provided and are not treated as cash spend.
No dollar value is assigned to participant outcomes, sales influence, avoided travel, or future reuse.
